pages.ja:
多くの人間の死体を見た。
その時に自分は死んで、新しく生まれたのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
多くの人間の死体を見た。
その時に自分は死んで、新しく生まれたのだ。
pages.en:
—I saw the bodies of countless people.

That was when I died,

and was born anew.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I saw many corpses.
I died at that time and was reborn.

pages.ja:
道に懺悔はなく。
目はそこで憎悪をなくし、
手はそこで憤怒をなくし、
足はそこで希望をなくし、
我はそこで自身をなくした。
pages.jaRuby:
道に懺悔はなく。
目はそこで憎悪をなくし、
手はそこで憤怒をなくし、
足はそこで希望をなくし、
我はそこで自身をなくした。
pages.en:
There was no repentance upon that road.

My eyes lost their hatred there.

My hands lost their fury there.

My feet lost their hope there.

And there, I lost myself.
pages.mirrorMoon:
I do not have any regrets.
My eyes lost hatred there.
My hands lost anger there.
My legs lost hope there.
My self lost its self there.

pages.ja:
何もなくなった。
助けてくれるモノなどいないと受け入れたのは、諦めからではない。
ただ、それが自然なのだと知っただけ。
死に行く者は死に、生きる者は生きるだけの話だ。
瓦礫の山に横たわって、広がる焼け跡を眺めていた。
そこで全てを理解した。
理解したつもりだった。
pages.jaRuby:
何もなくなった。
助けてくれるモノなどいないと受け入れたのは、諦めからではない。
ただ、それが自然なのだと知っただけ。
死に行く者は死に、生きる者は生きるだけの話だ。
瓦礫の山に横たわって、広がる焼け跡を眺めていた。
そこで全てを理解した。
理解したつもりだった。
pages.en:
Nothing remained.

I accepted that no one would save me, but not because I had surrendered to despair.

I merely learned that it was the natural state of things.

Those who are dying die. Those who will live, live. Nothing more.

I lay amid the rubble and looked out over the spreading ruin.

There, I understood everything.

Or believed that I did.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Everything went away.
It is not because I gave up that I believed nothing would save me.
I just found out that it’s natural.
It’s just that dying people will die and survivors will survive.
I laid down on the rubble and stared at the burning field.
I understood everything then.
I thought I understood everything.

pages.ja:
だが、それでも思ってしまった。
もしこの場で何もかもを救う事が出来るなら。
それは、どんなに素晴らしい事なのかと。
pages.jaRuby:
だが、それでも思ってしまった。
もしこの場で何もかもを救う事が出来るなら。
それは、どんなに素晴らしい事なのかと。
pages.en:
—And still, I could not keep myself from thinking.

If everything here could somehow be saved,

how wonderful a thing that would be.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But I still considered it…
How wonderful it would be…
If I was able to save everything here.

pages.ja:
憧れたのはそんな事だ。
ただ、誰も苦しまなければいいと思っただけ。
その為に正義の味方になろうとした。
なにしろ判りやすかったし、その在り方は理想のように思えたからだ。
pages.jaRuby:
憧れたのはそんな事だ。

その為に正義の味方になろうとした。
なにしろ判りやすかったし、その在り方は理想のように思えたからだ。
pages.en:
That was what I came to admire.

I only wanted no one to suffer.

For that reason, I tried to become a Hero of Justice.

The idea was simple to understand, and such a way of life seemed an ideal worth pursuing.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s what I admired.
I just wished nobody would have to suffer.
That’s why I tried to become a superhero.
It was simple, and it seemed like an ideal existence.

pages.ja:
だから目指した。
行き先は見えていて、道はそれこそ山ほどある。
何が正しいのか判らずとも、少しでも近づきたくて走り続けた。
pages.jaRuby:
だから目指した。
行き先は見えていて、道はそれこそ山ほどある。
何が正しいのか判らずとも、少しでも近づきたくて走り続けた。
pages.en:
So I pursued it.

I could see the destination, and there were more roads toward it than I could count.

Though I did not know which was right, I kept running in the hope of drawing even a little closer.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That was why I aimed for it.
I knew where I had to be, but there were many ways to get there.
I kept on running, wanting to get as close to it as possible, even though I did not know what was right or wrong.

pages.ja:
そうして通り過ぎた道の多くは歪んでいて、行き先は離れていく一方だ。
ひどい遠回りばかりしている。
切嗣に助けられてから十年間、ずっとそんな事の繰り返しだ。
pages.jaRuby:
そうして通り過ぎた道の多くは歪んでいて、行き先は離れていく一方だ。
ひどい遠回りばかりしている。
切嗣に助けられてから十年間、ずっとそんな事の繰り返しだ。
pages.en:
Many of the roads I passed through were twisted, and my destination only receded farther into the distance.

Every path has been a terrible detour.

For ten years, ever since Kiritsugu saved me, I have repeated the same thing.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Many paths I took were crooked, and my destination was only getting farther away.
I’m taking the long way.
I’ve been repeating this for ten years since I got saved by Kiritsugu.

pages.ja:
だが後悔はしない。
俺は遠坂のように器用じゃない。
選んだ道が過ちで、多くの物を失う時だってある。
それを無意味と切り捨てる事はできない。
踏みつけにしてきたもの、もう戻らないものの為にも、生き延びた意味を示さなければならない。
pages.jaRuby:
だが後悔はしない。
俺は遠坂のように器用じゃない。
選んだ道が過ちで、多くの物を失う時だってある。

踏みつけにしてきたもの、もう戻らないものの為にも、生き延びた意味を示さなければならない。
pages.en:
But I will not regret it.

I am not as deft as Tohsaka.

Sometimes the path I choose is wrong, and I lose many things along it.

I cannot simply discard those losses as meaningless.

For the sake of everything I have trampled underfoot, for the sake of everything that can never return, I must prove that my survival possessed meaning.
pages.mirrorMoon:
But I won’t regret it.
I’m not as skillful as Tohsaka.
I will take the wrong path and lose a lot of things at times.
But I cannot discard them as meaningless.
I have to present meanings for everything I’ve trampled upon and everything that cannot be returned.

pages.ja:
その為には、負けられない。
他人に負けるのは仕方がない。
けど自分には勝てる。諦めろと囁く自分にだけは、いつだって抗える。
誓ったのはその程度の事だ。
俺が信じたもの、信じたかったものは、一つだけ。
pages.jaRuby:
その為には、負けられない。

けど自分には勝てる。諦めろと囁く自分にだけは、いつだって抗える。
誓ったのはその程度の事だ。

pages.en:
To do that, I cannot lose.

Other people may defeat me. That is beyond my control.

But I can defeat myself. I can always resist the self that whispers for me to give up.

That is all I swore.

There was only one thing I believed—one thing I wanted to believe.
pages.mirrorMoon:
So I cannot lose.
It can’t be helped if I lose against someone else.
But I can win against myself. I can always fight back against my mind that tells me to give up.
That’s all I swore upon.
There’s only one thing that I believed in and wanted to believe in.

pages.ja:
……そう。
たとえ、俺自身が間違っていたとしても。
それを信じた事に、後悔だけはしないように。
pages.jaRuby:
……そう。
たとえ、[ruby text=このみち char=3]俺自身が間違っていたとしても。
それを信じた事に、後悔だけはしないように。
pages.en:
…Yes.

Even if *I myself—this path of mine* was wrong,

I would at least never regret having believed in it.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…That’s right.
Even if I am walking down the wrong path, I will not regret believing in it.

“The forest is deep and vast after refusing human intrusion for so many years. You've heard the stories, haven't you? Every year, several people wander inside unprepared and never find their way out.”

“All right. We’re heading to the forest on the outskirts of this town.
It’s a huge woodland, unkempt and far from the city.
It has rejected human interaction for a long time, so the forest is big and wide. You know how there are a few people every year that get lost in there for going in without any preparations, right?”

“——”

I nod without speaking.

Our destination is the Einzbern villa, located somewhere in that forest.

If our negotiations with Illyasviel break down and battle begins, our fate is sealed.

We will be unable to call for help, and escape will scarcely be possible.

Unless we defeat that giant—Berserker—we will never leave the forest alive.

—An hour's taxi ride from the city.

We follow the national highway over several mountains before reaching the edge of the forest.

Naturally, there is no paved road leading inside.

We leave the highway—a road scarcely different from an expressway—and walk another kilometer through scrub before finally reaching the entrance.

Of course, the forest does not have any paved roads.

pages.jaRuby: 「別に問題ないんじゃない？ わたしたちは奇襲にきた訳じゃないもの。話し合いにきたんだから、むしろ今からアピールしておいた方が得でしょ」

pages.mirrorMoon: “I don’t think it’ll be a problem. We didn’t come here for a surprise attack. We came to talk, so it would be in our favor to let them know we’re coming.”

「わかってるわかってる。士郎の見てたからどんなものか判ってるって
」
ひらひらと手を振って、堂々と森に踏み入る遠坂。
とたん。

pages.en:
“Oh. Be careful anyway. It gives you a little shock.”

“I know, I know. I watched what happened to you, so I know exactly what to expect—”

Waving one hand carelessly, Tohsaka marches into the forest.

The instant she does—
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Oh. Be careful though. It’ll shock you a bit.”
“I know, I know. I can tell how bad it is by looking at you”
She waves her hand and steps into the forest.
Then.

pages.ja:
「うきゃーーーー！」
なんて、愉快な奇声をあげて遠坂は跳び退いた。
pages.jaRuby:
「うきゃーーーー！」
なんて、愉快な奇声をあげて遠坂は跳び退いた。
pages.en:
“Eeeeeek———!”

With that remarkably entertaining shriek, Tohsaka leaps backward.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“UKYAAAAAAAAAAAA!!!”
Tohsaka jumps back with a funny scream.

pages.ja:
「うわあ……」
ばすばすという音。
遠坂の足下、積もった落ち葉が焼け焦げて見えるのは気のせいだと思いたい。

pages.en:
“Whoa…”

There is a rapid series of crackles.

I would like to believe that the fallen leaves beneath Tohsaka's feet only *appear* to be charred.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Wow…”
I hear fire hissing.
I want to believe it’s my imagination that the leaves under Tohsaka’s feet are scorched.

冷静に状況を解説する。
「く

」

pages.en:
“…It must be an alarm that varies from person to person. For me, it was barely a greeting.”

I provide a calm analysis of the situation.

“Kh—khkhkh—”

But my words do not seem to reach Tohsaka.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I guess there’s personal differences on the alarm. It was light in my case.”
I calmly analyze the situation.
“Kuhkuku, kukuku”
But it doesn’t seem like Tohsaka is listening to me.

pages.ja: 「やってくれるじゃないあのガキ……！ いま笑ったの、たしかに聞こえたんだから……！」
pages.jaRuby: 「やってくれるじゃないあのガキ……！ いま笑ったの、たしかに聞こえたんだから……！」
pages.en: “That little brat has some nerve…! I heard her laughing just now. I know I did…!”
pages.mirrorMoon: “That does it, kid…! I heard you laughing…!”

pages.en:
Tohsaka roars at the empty air.

Whatever happened to what she said a moment ago? She looks ready for a fight to the death, not a peaceful discussion.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Tohsaka yells into the empty sky.
She’s so angry that she might go to fight instead of talk.

I should remember that insulting Tohsaka appears to be fatal, no matter how far away she is.

It seems talking bad about Tohsaka is fatal no matter how far away you are from her, so I guess I’ll refrain from doing so.
